body:
One more small group for the same game, same rules and format as before (plain text only, nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, ASCII only, no em-dash, 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders). Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ireena travels with the party and does not fight: enemies go round her like water round a stone and she never strikes, and she hates standing back. Her short road lines (one line, spoken after a won fight by whoever is along) were written when she was a fighter. Two of them have to be redrafted for someone who watched from behind the line, and two more written. Then four Narrator lines for the middle of a fight.

## What I need

ROAD LINES (Ireena x1 each; spoken aloud on the road after a fight is won; under 28 words; she has just watched the fight and could not answer a blow):
- fight_glass: replaces "I'm not made of glass. I'm made of whatever's left when the glass breaks, and it held." She is not made of glass, and says she would rather the blow had come to her than be kept back from it.
- fight_father: replaces "Father taught me the sword so I'd never need it. He was a good man and a terrible prophet." Her father taught her the sword so she would not need it; the valley has decided she will not use it.
- fight_count: new. She counted the blows from behind the line, and knows which landed where; a grim, exact joke about being the party's ledger.
- fight_carry: new. She asks for anything to carry, bind, hold or watch: anything but waiting.
(Keep "Is anyone hurt? Say it plainly. I'd rather know now than at the next door." as it is; do not rewrite it.)

NARRATOR LINES MID-FIGHT (Narrator x1 each; one sentence, under 15 words; spoken while a fight is on and Ireena stands behind the party; third person about her, present tense; they must not say she attacks, shoots, is hit or is in danger; nothing touches her):
- keeps_back_warning: she shouts a warning at the party's back, and means it.
- keeps_back_name: she calls a name across the din and the swordsman turns in time.
- keeps_back_stone: she picks up a stone and weighs it in her hand, and puts it down again.
- keeps_back_lamp: she holds up a lamp (or torch) for those who are fighting by it.

That is 4 road lines and 4 Narrator lines.

## Voice reminders

IREENA: direct and proud; short sentences; dry humour with an edge; never names the devil, says "him", "the devil" or "our visitor"; pet phrases "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly." (once each at most).
NARRATOR (combat lines): one sentence, concrete, present tense, old gothic storyteller; no game terms; never cruel. Existing ones, so you hear them (do NOT repeat): "Ireena's knuckles whiten on her sheathed hilt as she steps clear of the steel." / "Hungry eyes slide right past Ireena to fix on you alone." / "Ireena folds her arms over her cloak, watching every blow she cannot answer." / "Not one blade angles toward Ireena where she waits." / "Ireena measures the distance between your back and the dark with level eyes."

## Canon limits

No new names or history. Do not name Strahd. She never strikes, is struck, shoots or throws anything at a foe in these lines.
result:
~ fight_glass
Ireena [defiant]: I'm not made of glass. I would rather take the blow myself than stand behind you and watch it fall.

~ fight_father
Ireena [bitter]: Father taught me the sword so I'd never need it. Now the whole valley has decided I'm not allowed to use it.

~ fight_count
Ireena [dry]: Seven blows given, three taken on the left flank. If I can't draw steel, I can at least keep the ledger.

~ fight_carry
Ireena [tense]: Give me a wound to bind, a pack to carry, or a corner to watch. Anything but standing idle while you bleed.

~ keeps_back_warning
Narrator [tense]: Ireena's sharp warning cuts through the clash of steel to guard your blind side.

~ keeps_back_name
Narrator [urgent]: Ireena calls out across the din, and a blade turns just in time.

~ keeps_back_stone
Narrator [somber]: Ireena weighs a heavy road-stone in her palm before letting it drop back to the dirt.

~ keeps_back_lamp
Narrator [steady]: Ireena holds the lantern high, casting steady light across the ground where you fight.
